result.topic_en: Euler treats the sixth order of his singular double series (m+n=7): from the case m=6, n=1 he derives the value of the double sum ∫1/z^6(1/y) in terms of simple sums, and he begins the case m=5, n=2.
result.transcription:
SERIES SINGVLARES. 157
Ordo sextus, quo $m+n=7$.
16. Sit primo $m=6$ et $n=1$, eritque
$\int\frac{1}{z^6}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z}-\int\frac{1}{z^7}=$
$2\int\frac{1}{z^6}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z}-\int\frac{1}{z^6}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)$
$-2\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^5}=2\int\frac{1}{z^4}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^3}-2\int\frac{1}{z^6}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z}$
$+\int\frac{1}{z}\left(\frac{1}{y^6}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^2}\left(\frac{1}{y^5}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y^4}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^4}\left(\frac{1}{y^3}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^5}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^6}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)$
vnde colligimus hanc aequationem
$\int\frac{1}{z}\left(\frac{1}{y^6}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^2}\left(\frac{1}{y^5}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y^4}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^4}\left(\frac{1}{y^3}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^5}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)=$
$\int\frac{1}{z^6}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z}+2\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^5}+2\int\frac{1}{z^4}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^3}-\int\frac{1}{z^7}.$
Cum vero sit
$\int\frac{1}{z}\left(\frac{1}{y^6}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^6}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)=\int\frac{1}{z^6}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z}+\int\frac{1}{z^7}$ erit
$\int\frac{1}{z^2}\left(\frac{1}{y^5}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y^4}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^4}\left(\frac{1}{y^3}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^5}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)-\int\frac{1}{z^6}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)=$
$2\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^5}+2\int\frac{1}{z^4}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^3}-2\int\frac{1}{z^7}.$
Est vero etiam
$\int\frac{1}{z^2}\left(\frac{1}{y^5}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^5}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)=\int\frac{1}{z^5}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^2}+\int\frac{1}{z^7}$ et
$\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y^4}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^4}\left(\frac{1}{y^3}\right)=\int\frac{1}{z^4}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^3}+\frac{1}{z^7}$
vnde habebitur
$\int\frac{1}{z^6}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)=4\int\frac{1}{z^7}-\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^5}-\int\frac{1}{z^4}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^3}$
Sit secundo $m=5$ et $n=2$, eritque $\int\frac{1}{z^5}\int\frac{1}{z^2}-\int\frac{1}{z^7}=$
$-10\int\frac{1}{z^6}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z}+\int\frac{1}{z^5}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)+5\int\frac{1}{z^6}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)$
$+2\int\frac{1}{z^2}\int\frac{1}{z^5}+6\int\frac{1}{z^4}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^3}+10\int\frac{1}{z^6}\int\frac{1}{z}$
$-\int\frac{1}{z^2}\left(\frac{1}{y^5}\right)-2\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y^4}\right)-3\int\frac{1}{z^4}\left(\frac{1}{y^3}\right)-4\int\frac{1}{z^5}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)-5\int\frac{1}{z^6}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)$
vnde colligitur haec aequatio :
V 3 $\int\frac{1}{z^2}$

items.english: whence one will have: the double sum ∫1/z^6(1/y) equals 4∫1/z^7 − ∫1/z^2·∫1/z^5 − ∫1/z^4·∫1/z^3.
Let secondly m=5 and n=2; then ∫1/z^5·∫1/z^2 − ∫1/z^7 will equal [the expression that follows], from which an equation is derived.
